brief.subject: Diesel jumps 7.6 cents, SoCal port strike looms, PMI hits 55.5
brief.headline: Diesel Climbs 7.6 Cents as Port Strike Threat Builds and Manufacturing Grows
brief.dek: Fuel costs rise, a Southern California port strike nears, factories keep expanding, and holiday parcel demand points up.
brief.lede: Diesel rose 7.6 cents to $6.352 per gallon, squeezing margins for anyone without a strong fuel surcharge.

sections.heading: Diesel Jumps Again
bullets: $6.352 per gallon is the national diesel average for the week of 2026-10-26, per EIA.
Up 7.6 cents (1.2%) week over week, enough to erase thin margins on long hauls.
Down 3.0 cents over four weeks, so the latest jump reverses most of the recent relief.
Check that your fuel surcharge tables track weekly moves, not monthly averages.

sections.heading: SoCal Port Strike Days Away
bullets: A strike at the busiest U.S. port could hit within days as union watchmen and port employers keep negotiating.
Both sides extended the contract, which buys time but does not settle anything yet.
Drayage and Southern California outbound carriers should plan for possible container delays and lane disruption.

sections.heading: Factories Keep Growing
bullets: 55.5 was October's ISM manufacturing PMI, beating expectations and marking a 10th straight month of expansion.
Steady factory output supports industrial and flatbed freight demand heading into year end.
Survey respondents grew more negative, citing the Iran war, price swings and trade wars as risks.
Public LTL carriers describe demand with cautious optimism, matching the PMI signal.

sections.heading: Peak Season Signals
bullets: 4% growth in holiday parcel demand is forecast by ShipMatrix, the strongest peak since 2022.
Big retailers, including Amazon, reported paying more for freight in the third quarter.
Rising shipper freight costs plus firmer peak volume may give small carriers more room on rates.

sections.heading: Network Shifts to Watch
bullets: Norfolk Southern and Schneider National are partnering to expand East Coast intermodal reach, adding rail competition on some lanes.
$400M Walmart distribution center planned for Cibolo, Texas, with groundbreaking expected this February.
The 744,000-plus-square-foot site could create new regional freight in the San Antonio area.
